commit.message:
feat(assemblyai): add assemblyai-stt-3-7 transcription and assemblyai-tts-1 speech models (#25321)

## Background

AssemblyAI released
[AssemblyAI-STT-3.7](https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/pre-recorded-audio/select-the-speech-model)
(`assemblyai-stt-3-7`) as its flagship pre-recorded speech-to-text
model, deprecated `universal-3-5-pro` and `universal-3-pro`, and
launched a [text-to-speech
API](https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/tts/api-reference/http-api/create-speech)
(`assemblyai-tts-1`). The AssemblyAI API also no longer accepts the
singular `speech_model` request parameter (used by the legacy `best`
model) or the `slam-1` model.

`@ai-sdk/assemblyai` only supported transcription, still recommended
`universal-3-5-pro`, and sent `best` through the rejected `speech_model`
parameter.

## Summary

Transcription:

- Add `assemblyai-stt-3-7` to the model catalog, with prompting,
keyterms, `temperature`, and `removeAudioTags` support (the same option
set as Universal-3.5 Pro).
- `universal-3-5-pro` now emits a `deprecated` warning pointing to
`assemblyai-stt-3-7`. The `universal-2` notice points to
`assemblyai-stt-3-7` and notes that `universal-2` remains available for
languages it does not support.
- Remove the `best` model ID and the legacy `speech_model` request path,
and stop listing `universal-3-pro`. These IDs (and `slam-1`) are now
sent through `speech_models` like any other ID, without special
handling, so the API's error lists the accepted models.

Speech (new):

- Add `assemblyai.speech()` / `speechModel()` for `POST
https://tts.us.assemblyai.com/v1/speech`, implementing `SpeechModelV4`.
- `voice` maps to `voice_id`; `language` maps ISO 639-1 codes (`en`,
`es`, `de`, `it`, `pt`, `fr`) to the API's language names;
`outputFormat` supports `mp3` (default), `wav`, `pcm`, `mulaw`, and
`alaw`.
- Provider options: `encoding`, `container`, `sampleRate`, `bitRate`.
Options that do not apply to the resolved encoding are ignored with a
warning, as are unsupported languages, `speed` other than `1`, and
`instructions`.
- Requests are buffered (`stream: false`), so the response reports the
final `X-TTS-Billed-Characters` and `X-TTS-Audio-Duration-Ms`. These are
returned as `usage: { characters }` and in `providerMetadata.assemblyai`
together with the request id, model, voice, language, encoding, and
sample rate.

Docs, the generated capability tables, the core transcription and speech
model tables, the README, and the examples (including a new
`generate-speech/assemblyai/basic.ts`) are updated.

## End-to-End Verification

Exercised the real AssemblyAI pre-recorded transcription and
text-to-speech APIs through the public `generateSpeech` and `transcribe`
functions, using this checkout's locally built packages.

Prerequisite: an AssemblyAI API key in `ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY` (not
included).

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=ai... --filter=@ai-sdk/assemblyai...
cd examples/ai-functions
node --input-type=module < /tmp/assemblyai-e2e.mjs
```

`/tmp/assemblyai-e2e.mjs` (run from `examples/ai-functions`, so `ai` and
`@ai-sdk/assemblyai` resolve to the workspace packages):

```js
import { assemblyai } from '@ai-sdk/assemblyai';
import { generateSpeech, transcribe } from 'ai';

globalThis.AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS = false;

const speech = await generateSpeech({
  model: assemblyai.speech('assemblyai-tts-1'),
  text: 'Hello from the AI SDK. This is a short AssemblyAI text to speech test.',
  voice: 'aai-kyla',
});
const { requestId, ...speechMetadata } = speech.providerMetadata.assemblyai;
console.log('generateSpeech assemblyai-tts-1');
console.log('  mediaType:', speech.audio.mediaType);
console.log('  warnings:', JSON.stringify(speech.warnings));
console.log('  providerMetadata.assemblyai:', JSON.stringify(speechMetadata));

for (const modelId of [
  'assemblyai-stt-3-7',
  'universal-2',
  'universal-3-5-pro',
  'best',
]) {
  try {
    const result = await transcribe({
      model: assemblyai.transcription(modelId),
      audio: speech.audio.uint8Array,
    });
    const body = result.responses[0].body;
    console.log(`transcribe ${modelId}`);
    console.log('  text:', result.text);
    console.log('  durationInSeconds:', result.durationInSeconds);
    console.log('  speech_model_used:', body.speech_model_used);
    console.log('  warnings:', JSON.stringify(result.warnings.map(w => w.type)));
  } catch (error) {
    console.log(`transcribe ${modelId}`);
    console.log('  error:', error.statusCode, error.message);
  }
}
```

Observed output:

```text
generateSpeech assemblyai-tts-1
  mediaType: audio/mpeg
  warnings: []
  providerMetadata.assemblyai: {"model":"assemblyai-tts-1","voiceId":"aai-kyla","language":"english","encoding":"mp3","sampleRate":24000,"audioDurationMs":6240,"billedCharacters":70}
transcribe assemblyai-stt-3-7
  text: Hello from the AI SDK. This is a short AssemblyAI text-to-speech test.
  durationInSeconds: 7
  speech_model_used: assemblyai-stt-3-7
  warnings: []
transcribe universal-2
  text: Hello from the AI SDK. This is a short assembly AI text to speech test.
  durationInSeconds: 7
  speech_model_used: universal-2
  warnings: ["other"]
transcribe universal-3-5-pro
  text: Hello from the AI SDK. This is a short AssemblyAI text-to-speech test.
  durationInSeconds: 7
  speech_model_used: universal-3-5-pro
  warnings: ["deprecated"]
transcribe best
  error: 400 "speech_models" must be a non-empty list containing one or more of: "assemblyai-stt-3-7", "universal-3-5-pro", "universal-2"
```

The speech call returned playable MP3 audio with the billed character
count equal to the input length (70), and transcribing it with
`assemblyai-stt-3-7` ran that model (`speech_model_used`) and recovered
the text. Before this change, `best` was sent as `speech_model: 'best'`,

## Background

AssemblyAI released
[AssemblyAI-STT-3.7](https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/pre-recorded-audio/select-the-speech-model)
(`assemblyai-stt-3-7`) as its flagship pre-recorded speech-to-text
model, deprecated `universal-3-5-pro` and `universal-3-pro`, and
launched a [text-to-speech
API](https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/tts/api-reference/http-api/create-speech)
(`assemblyai-tts-1`). The AssemblyAI API also no longer accepts the
singular `speech_model` request parameter (used by the legacy `best`
model) or the `slam-1` model.

`@ai-sdk/assemblyai` only supported transcription, still recommended
`universal-3-5-pro`, and sent `best` through the rejected `speech_model`
parameter.

## Summary

Transcription:

- Add `assemblyai-stt-3-7` to the model catalog, with prompting,
keyterms, `temperature`, and `removeAudioTags` support (the same option
set as Universal-3.5 Pro).
- `universal-3-5-pro` now emits a `deprecated` warning pointing to
`assemblyai-stt-3-7`. The `universal-2` notice points to
`assemblyai-stt-3-7` and notes that `universal-2` remains available for
languages it does not support.
- Remove the `best` model ID and the legacy `speech_model` request path,
and stop listing `universal-3-pro`. These IDs (and `slam-1`) are now
sent through `speech_models` like any other ID, without special
handling, so the API's error lists the accepted models.

Speech (new):

- Add `assemblyai.speech()` / `speechModel()` for `POST
https://tts.us.assemblyai.com/v1/speech`, implementing `SpeechModelV4`.
- `voice` maps to `voice_id`; `language` maps ISO 639-1 codes (`en`,
`es`, `de`, `it`, `pt`, `fr`) to the API's language names;
`outputFormat` supports `mp3` (default), `wav`, `pcm`, `mulaw`, and
`alaw`.
- Provider options: `encoding`, `container`, `sampleRate`, `bitRate`.
Options that do not apply to the resolved encoding are ignored with a
warning, as are unsupported languages, `speed` other than `1`, and
`instructions`.
- Requests are buffered (`stream: false`), so the response reports the
final `X-TTS-Billed-Characters` and `X-TTS-Audio-Duration-Ms`. These are
returned as `usage: { characters }` and in `providerMetadata.assemblyai`
together with the request id, model, voice, language, encoding, and
sample rate.

Docs, the generated capability tables, the core transcription and speech
model tables, the README, and the examples (including a new
`generate-speech/assemblyai/basic.ts`) are updated.

## End-to-End Verification

Exercised the real AssemblyAI pre-recorded transcription and
text-to-speech APIs through the public `generateSpeech` and `transcribe`
functions, using this checkout's locally built packages.

Prerequisite: an AssemblyAI API key in `ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY` (not
included).

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=ai... --filter=@ai-sdk/assemblyai...
cd examples/ai-functions
node --input-type=module < /tmp/assemblyai-e2e.mjs
```

`/tmp/assemblyai-e2e.mjs` (run from `examples/ai-functions`, so `ai` and
`@ai-sdk/assemblyai` resolve to the workspace packages):

```js
import { assemblyai } from '@ai-sdk/assemblyai';
import { generateSpeech, transcribe } from 'ai';

globalThis.AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS = false;

const speech = await generateSpeech({
  model: assemblyai.speech('assemblyai-tts-1'),
  text: 'Hello from the AI SDK. This is a short AssemblyAI text to speech test.',
  voice: 'aai-kyla',
});

console.log('generateSpeech assemblyai-tts-1');
console.log('  mediaType:', speech.audio.mediaType);
console.log('  warnings:', JSON.stringify(speech.warnings));
console.log('  providerMetadata.assemblyai:', JSON.stringify(speechMetadata));

for (const modelId of [
  'assemblyai-stt-3-7',
  'universal-2',
  'universal-3-5-pro',
  'best',

    const result = await transcribe({
      model: assemblyai.transcription(modelId),
      audio: speech.audio.uint8Array,

    const body = result.responses[0].body;
    console.log(`transcribe ${modelId}`);
    console.log('  text:', result.text);
    console.log('  durationInSeconds:', result.durationInSeconds);
    console.log('  speech_model_used:', body.speech_model_used);
    console.log('  warnings:', JSON.stringify(result.warnings.map(w => w.type)));
  } catch (error) {
    console.log(`transcribe ${modelId}`);
    console.log('  error:', error.statusCode, error.message);
  }
}

Version Packages (#25229)

This PR was opened by the [Changesets
release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When
you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will
be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release
yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will
be updated.


# Releases
## ai@7.0.178

### Patch Changes

- 0b8cbfa: `generateText` and `streamText` passed the messages array
that `prepareStep` returned to tools and tool approval functions as it
was. When `prepareStep` returned the same array for several steps or
calls, tool approval functions could not tell the tool calls of one
model response from the tool calls of another. The messages array of
every step is now created for that step, so the messages that
`prepareStep` returns are copied.
- 6815153: fix(ai): forward the `preliminary` flag on provider-executed
tool results in `streamText`, so preliminary results (e.g. OpenAI image
generation previews) are no longer recorded as final tool results in
step content and response messages
- 15bfd6b: add telemetry, runtime context and lifecycle callbacks to
`experimental_extract`
- 15bfd6b: redact file urls from download errors sent to telemetry
- 2613bb4: fix(ai): build the `ai`, `ai/internal`, and `ai/test`
entrypoints together so their types stay compatible with each other
- 63593a7: With `experimental_toolApprovalSecret` configured,
`generateText` and `streamText` signed the approval request of a tool
call that the tool approval policy had denied automatically. A client
that controls the message history could send that request back with an
approved response and have the denied tool call executed. Approval
requests of automatically denied tool calls are no longer signed, so
such a response is rejected with `AI_InvalidToolApprovalSignatureError`.

Signatures that earlier versions issued for automatic denials stay
valid. To invalidate them, rotate the secret passed to
`experimental_toolApprovalSecret`. Approval requests that are still
waiting for a user decision then have to be requested again.

# Releases
## ai@7.0.178

### Patch Changes

- 0b8cbfa: `generateText` and `streamText` passed the messages array
that `prepareStep` returned to tools and tool approval functions as it
was. When `prepareStep` returned the same array for several steps or
calls, tool approval functions could not tell the tool calls of one
model response from the tool calls of another. The messages array of
every step is now created for that step, so the messages that
`prepareStep` returns are copied.
- 6815153: fix(ai): forward the `preliminary` flag on provider-executed
tool results in `streamText`, so preliminary results (e.g. OpenAI image
generation previews) are no longer recorded as final tool results in
step content and response messages
- 15bfd6b: add telemetry, runtime context and lifecycle callbacks to
`experimental_extract`
- 15bfd6b: redact file urls from download errors sent to telemetry
- 2613bb4: fix(ai): build the `ai`, `ai/internal`, and `ai/test`
entrypoints together so their types stay compatible with each other
- 63593a7: With `experimental_toolApprovalSecret` configured,
`generateText` and `streamText` signed the approval request of a tool
call that the tool approval policy had denied automatically. A client
that controls the message history could send that request back with an
approved response and have the denied tool call executed. Approval
requests of automatically denied tool calls are no longer signed, so
such a response is rejected with `AI_InvalidToolApprovalSignatureError`.

Signatures that earlier versions issued for automatic denials stay
valid. To invalidate them, rotate the secret passed to
`experimental_toolApprovalSecret`. Approval requests that are still
waiting for a user decision then have to be requested again.

commit.message:
chore(ci): install only the MCP package's dependencies on Windows (#25289)

## Background

- windows job only runs `@ai-sdk/mcp`'s tests but it installs every
package in the repo and caches the full pnpm store
- on a recent `main` push it took 210s in total, but almost all of it
was just writing files:

- downloading the 1.1 GB store cache: 6s
- unpacking it: 50s
- `pnpm install` (linking 3,873 packages): 71s
- saving the store again (`main` only): 53s

Without the cache, setup took 85s, so the cache made the job slower.

## Summary

- `pnpm/setup` no longer runs its own install or caches the store
- a separate step runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter
"@ai-sdk/mcp..."`, which installs MCP, its workspace dependencies and
the root (for `turbo`): 539 packages instead of 3,873

### Results

| Windows job | Before (`main`) | After (cache hits) | After (`--force`,
nothing cached) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Setup pnpm and Node.js | 131s | 7s | 5s |
| Install dependencies | (part of setup) | 9s | 7s |
| Run Windows tests | ~2s | 1s | 18s |
| Save the pnpm store | 53s | — | — |
| **Whole job** | **210s** | **38s** | **50s** |

The `--force` run was a temporary commit (reverted) to make sure the
tests really run against the smaller install on Windows, not just replay
from the cache.

commit.message:
chore(ci): run CI through Turborepo and Vercel CI (#25242)

## Background

- CI was overly complicated
- Split across a long GitHub Actions workflow, hand-written path
filters, build artifacts passed between jobs, and shards.
- Most PRs start 48 jobs that each spend 30-90s installing dependencies
- Several checks ran outside Turborepo so they weren't cached
  - `tsc --build` over the entire repo, which was ~4m on every PR
  - `ai` and codemod tests, because they were sharded
- Path filters missed checks that should have run
- `packages/rsc` tests didn't run when `ai` changed even though it's a
dependency - only when rsc itself changed
  - node 24 and 26 tests skipped lockfile and dependency bumps

## Summary

Move CI into `turbo.json` and run as much as possible on [Vercel
CI](https://vercel.com/docs/ci), which runs every task on its own
machine and skips tasks whose inputs don't change.

GitHub Actions remain, for now, for the things Vercel CI can't do: Node
22/26 and Windows MCP tests.

### Every check is a Turborepo task

| Check | Task |
| --- | --- |
| Builds (packages and all examples) | `build` |
| Type-check | `type-check` (per package) |
| Tests (all packages, including `ai` and codemod, no sharding) | `test`
|
| RSC and devtools Playwright tests (devtools e2e wasn't in CI before) |
`test:browser` |
| Bundle size | `ai#check-bundle-size` |
| Zod 3 / Zod 4 consumer bundles | `ai-sdk-bundler-tests#test:bundlers`
|
| Load time | `ai-sdk-load-time#test:load-time` |
| Docs site tests | `ai-sdk-docs#test:site` (reads `content/**`) |
| Lint, verifiers, docs and model-capability validation, tarball tool
tests, konsistent | uncached root tasks |

also:
- upgraded Turborepo from 2.9.14 to 2.11.11, which adds task tags
- enable `strictTaskEntrypointSelection`
- this makes packages without a script for a task not pull in that
task's dependencies
- the bundler and load-time checks are now small workspace packages
(`tools/bundler-tests`, `tools/load-time`), so Turborepo tracks the
packages they depend on
- `pnpm test:bundlers` now runs through Turborepo, so it builds the
packages it tests first
- the load-time limits are raised to fit Vercel CI's machines, since
timings vary by up to ~30% between runs
- the two MCP example route tests are now `@example/next-openai`'s
`test` script
- `turbo.json` files are now formatted by oxfmt (they were in its ignore
list)

### Type-check per package

- each package runs `tsc --noEmit` itself so that results are cached per
package
- removed TS project references, `composite`, the root `tsconfig.json`
and `tsconfig.with-examples.json`, `update-references`, and the
`tsconfig.build.json` files that only disabled `composite`.
- also removed `*.tsbuildinfo` from `clean` scripts, since packages no
longer produce them
- next.js examples rely on `next build` which already type checks

### `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is much smaller

github actions only has two jobs:

- `Node 22` / `Node 26`: `turbo run test`
- `Windows`: `turbo run test:windows`

it also now saves the pnpm store only on `main`.

### Slack alerts cover Vercel CI

Vercel CI reports a commit status instead of running a workflow, so
`slack-workflow-failure-notification.yml` now also listens for `status`
events. A `Vercel CI` failure on `main` or a `release-v*` branch sends
one Slack message per run.

### other fixes

these were found by the stricter checks above

- the `ai`, `ai/internal` and `ai/test` entrypoints were built
separately
- this meant each entrypoint shipped its own copy of the type
declarations.
- augmenting the interfaces of `ai` (like harness does for
`CallWarningRegistry`) didn't apply to the `ai/internal` copy, so a
`StepResult` from `ai` wasn't assignable to one from `ai/internal`
  - they're now built as one graph with shared chunks.
  - this also removes about 136 KB of code duplicated into `ai/internal`
- `examples/harness-e2e-next` now builds with Turbopack
  - the webpack build was actually broken at runtime 
- `examples/sveltekit-openai`: added a missing `await` on
`convertToModelMessages`.
- `@ai-sdk/code-mode`: fixed type errors in test files that CI never
type-checked, and the tests now import from source instead of the
package's own build.
- `@ai-sdk/harness-pi`: the two grep tests that rely on `chmod 0` skip
when running as root, since root ignores file permissions (they still
run in the Node 22/26 jobs).
- `ai`: the declaration-emit test gets a 30s timeout, like
`global.test.ts`, since loading TypeScript can exceed the default 5s on
a busy runner.
- `examples/nest`: sets `rootDir` explicitly now that `composite` is
gone.

## Checklist

- [x] All commits are signed (PRs with unsigned commits cannot be
merged)
- [x] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug
fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)
- [X] I have reviewed this pull request (self-review)

## Future Work

Before merging:

- update the branch with `main`, so Vercel CI checks the merged code
- update the required status checks for `main`:
- Remove `TypeScript`, `test`, `Lint & Format` and `Bundle Size Check`.
  - Add `Vercel CI`, `Node 22`, `Node 26` and `Windows`.

follow ups:
- add verifier to enforce all packages having type check scripts
- make `ai`'s provider-specific tests generic (test against the spec)
and/or move them into an integration tests package; this also stops
`ai#build` waiting on providers it only uses in tests
- revisit the GitHub Actions Node jobs if they get too slow on cold runs
(8-10 min when everything rebuilds)
- if the load-time check gets flaky, print min/median/max to see whether
the noise is within a run or between machines

feat(ai): add telemetry and lifecycle callbacks to experimental_extract (#25232)

## background

`experimental_extract` shipped without telemetry, `runtimeContext` or
`onStart` / `onEnd`, same as decide's first pr. this adds them the same
way #21162 did for decide, matching how decide works today (context
allowlists, `aiVersion`, recording flags in the tracing channel)

## summary

- add `telemetry`, `runtimeContext`, `onStart` and `onEnd` to
`experimental_extract`
- add `Experimental_ExtractStartEvent`, `Experimental_ExtractEndEvent`,
`Experimental_ExtractionModelCallStartEvent` and
`Experimental_ExtractionModelCallEndEvent`
- add `experimental_onExtractStart`,
`experimental_onExtractionModelCallStart`,
`experimental_onExtractionModelCallEnd` and `experimental_onExtractEnd`
to telemetry integrations, kept out of the stable `onStart` / `onEnd`
unions like decide
- add an `experimental_extract` tracing channel span
- `OpenTelemetry` records an `extract {modelId}` operation span and a
child model call span with usage and response id. state, fields,
reference date and answers go under `ai.extraction.*` behind a new
opt-in `experimental_extraction` option
- hide extraction `fields` and `referenceDate` from integrations when
`recordInputs` is false, next to decide's `questions`. both go into the
model prompt. answers were already covered by the `answers` output rule
- keep request headers and provider options out of extract telemetry and
the tracing channel, since they can carry credentials like auth headers
or provider api keys. `onStart` / `onEnd` and the provider call still
get them
- replace file urls and provider file references in extraction state
with `[redacted]` for telemetry, since they can be signed links. the
download and `onStart` / `onEnd` still use the originals
- don't record provider metadata on extraction spans, it can hold
document content like ocr text. integrations still get it in the events
- redact the file url from download errors sent to telemetry, for every
operation. the error the app catches keeps the url
- docs for the telemetry and lifecycle callbacks pages, the
`experimental_extract` reference and a telemetry section in the
extractions guide, plus otel and tracing channel examples

same order as decide: invalid input and unsupported field types throw
before any event, a refusal fires `onError` and no end events, and the
model call end event has the normalized answers that are validated and
returned

left out on purpose: no `LegacyOpenTelemetry` support since legacy is
fading out, and no deprecated hook aliases since extract never had old
names

bundle limit goes from 661 to 664 kb, node is 662.87 kb

  status: { code: 0 }

  parentSpanContext: undefined
  name: 'extract gpt-6.2-sol'
  id: '0f3449a6acb52236'
  status: { code: 0 }
```

invalid api key:
threw: AI_APICallError
onError calls: 1
span extract gpt-6.2-sol status=2 events=exception
span extract gpt-6.2-sol status=2 events=exception

`experimental_extract`
- add `Experimental_ExtractStartEvent`, `Experimental_ExtractEndEvent`,
`Experimental_ExtractionModelCallStartEvent` and
`Experimental_ExtractionModelCallEndEvent`
- add `experimental_onExtractStart`,
`experimental_onExtractionModelCallStart`,
`experimental_onExtractionModelCallEnd` and `experimental_onExtractEnd`
to telemetry integrations, kept out of the stable `onStart` / `onEnd`
unions like decide
- add an `experimental_extract` tracing channel span
- `OpenTelemetry` records an `extract {modelId}` operation span and a
child model call span with usage and response id. state, fields,
reference date and answers go under `ai.extraction.*` behind a new
opt-in `experimental_extraction` option
- hide extraction `fields` and `referenceDate` from integrations when
`recordInputs` is false, next to decide's `questions`. both go into the
model prompt. answers were already covered by the `answers` output rule
- keep request headers and provider options out of extract telemetry and
the tracing channel, since they can carry credentials like auth headers
or provider api keys. `onStart` / `onEnd` and the provider call still
get them
- replace file urls and provider file references in extraction state
with `[redacted]` for telemetry, since they can be signed links. the
download and `onStart` / `onEnd` still use the originals
- don't record provider metadata on extraction spans, it can hold
document content like ocr text. integrations still get it in the events
- redact the file url from download errors sent to telemetry, for every
operation. the error the app catches keeps the url
- docs for the telemetry and lifecycle callbacks pages, the
`experimental_extract` reference and a telemetry section in the
extractions guide, plus otel and tracing channel examples

same order as decide: invalid input and unsupported field types throw
before any event, a refusal fires `onError` and no end events, and the
model call end event has the normalized answers that are validated and
returned

left out on purpose: no `LegacyOpenTelemetry` support since legacy is
fading out, and no deprecated hook aliases since extract never had old
names

bundle limit goes from 661 to 664 kb, node is 662.87 kb
